rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali held that intercourse with a married captive woman remained forbidden.
rows.anchor: فرجح علي كرم الله وجهه التحريم

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman held that a married captive woman became lawful to her captor.
rows.anchor: وعثمان رضي الله عنه التحليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers Ali because the permission verse is restricted to another case and unlawful status prevails when lawful and unlawful meet.
rows.anchor: وقول علي أظهر لأن آية التحليل مخصوصة في غير ذلك ولقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may attach to an implied consequence, or be disconnected and mean that past cases are forgiven by God's mercy.
rows.anchor: استثناء من لازم المعنى، أو منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protected women are women who have husbands, made chaste by marriage or by their husbands.
rows.anchor: ذوات الأزواج، أحصنهن التزويج أو الأزواج

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads the word with a kasra on ṣād throughout the Qur'an, because the women guarded their chastity.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بكسر الصاد في جميع القرآن لأنهن أحصن فروجهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means captured women whose non-Muslim husbands remained behind; captivity ends their marriage and makes them lawful to their captors.
rows.anchor: يريد ما ملكت أيمانكم من اللاتي سبين ولهن أزواج كفار فهن حلال للسابين، والنكاح مرتفع بالسبي

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that Muslims captured women with unbelieving husbands at Awtas, hesitated, asked the Prophet, then treated them as lawful after the verse came down.
rows.anchor: لقول أبي سعيد رضي الله تعالى عنه: أصبنا سبايا يوم أوطاس

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line about spears marrying a married woman illustrates the view that captivity ends the prior marriage.
rows.anchor:
الفرزدق بقوله:
وذات حليل أنكحتها رماحنا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa held that capturing both spouses does not dissolve their marriage or make the woman lawful to the captor.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة لو سبي الزوجان لم يرتفع النكاح ولم تحل للسابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Abu Hanifa's view, arguing that the unrestricted wording of the verse and report contradicts it.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الآية والحديث حجة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an emphatic verbal noun: God has prescribed these prohibitions as a written prescription.
rows.anchor: مصدر مؤكد، أي كتب الله عليكم تحريم هؤلاء كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with plural and nominative construction means these are God's prescribed duties upon you.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «كتب» الله بالجمع والرفع أي هذه فرائض الله عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has the phrase as a finite verb, written as wa-kataba Allah.
rows.anchor: «وكتب الله» بلفظ الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-uḥilla lakum coordinates with the implicit verb that governs kitab Allah.
rows.anchor: وأحل لكم } عطف على الفعل المضمر الذي نصب كتاب الله

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read wa-uḥilla in the passive, coordinating it with ḥurrimat.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم على البناء للمفعول عطفا على { حرمت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What lies beyond the eight prohibited categories listed above means everything besides those forbidden women.
rows.anchor: ما وراء ذلكم } ما سوى المحرمات الثمان المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sunna further excludes analogous milk-kin relations and combining a woman with her paternal or maternal aunt.
rows.anchor: وخص عنه بالسنة ما في معنى المذكورات كسائر محرمات الرضاع، والجمع بين المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause means seeking women with money spent on their dowries or purchase while remaining chaste rather than fornicating.
rows.anchor: مفعول له والمعنى أحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم إرادة أن تبتغوا النساء بأموالكم بالصرف في مهورهن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the object of seeking is omitted, or the phrase is an apposition to what lies beyond the prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن لا يقدر مفعول تبتغوا وكأنه قيل إرادة أن يصرفوا أموالكم محصنين غير مسافحين أو بدل مما وراء ذلك

rows.speaker: الحنفية
rows.claim: Hanafis cite this wording to argue that a dowry must consist of money.
rows.anchor: واحتج به الحنفية على أن المهر لا بد وأن يكون مالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the verse does not prove the Hanafi requirement that dowry must be monetary.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥṣān is chastity that protects the self from blame and punishment; sifāḥ is fornication, named for spilling semen.
rows.anchor: والإحصان العفة فإنها تحصين للنفس عن اللوم والعقاب، والسفاح الزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā istamtaʿtum means the women one enjoyed among those married to him.
rows.anchor: فمن تمتعتم به من المنكوحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, enjoyment refers to intercourse with the women or contracting marriage with them.
rows.anchor: أو فما استمتعتم به منهن من جماع أو عقد عليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wages are their dowries, since the dowry is payment in exchange for enjoyment.
rows.anchor: فآتوهن أجورهن } مهورهن فإن المهر في مقابلة الاستمتاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farīḍatan may be a circumstantial qualifier meaning prescribed, an adjective to an omitted verbal noun, or an emphatic verbal noun.
rows.anchor: فريضة } حال من الأجور بمعنى مفروضة، أو صفة مصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the prescribed dowry, the couple may mutually agree to increase or reduce it, or settle maintenance, residence, or separation.
rows.anchor: فيما يزاد على المسمى أو يحط عنه بالتراضي، أو فيما تراضيا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means an oath by the Lord; lā is an emphatic extra particle, also used in affirmative statements such as 90:1.
rows.anchor: فلا وربك } أي فوربك، ولا مزيدة لتأكيد القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputes are matters they differ over and intermingle; shajar evokes the intertwining branches of a tree.
rows.anchor: فيما اختلف بينهم واختلط ومنه الشجر لتداخل أغصانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finding no distress means no constriction over the judgment, whether from the ruling itself or from doubt, which leaves a doubter distressed.
rows.anchor: ضيقا مما حكمت به، أو من حكمك أو شكا من أجله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To submit fully is to comply with the Prophet both outwardly and inwardly.
rows.anchor: وينقادوا لك انقيادا بظاهرهم وباطنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to kill yourselves may mean exposing yourselves to death in jihad.
rows.anchor: تعرضوا بها للقتل في الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means literally killing one another, as the Israelites did.
rows.anchor: أو اقتلوها كما قتل بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an can be infinitival, or explanatory because katabna carries the meaning of commanding.
rows.anchor: وأن مصدرية أو مفسرة لأن كتبنا في معنى أمرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving their homes refers to the Israelites' departure when they were called to repent from worshipping the calf.
rows.anchor: خروجهم حين استتيبوا من عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read the nun in an-iqtulū with kasra, and pronounce the wāw of ukhrūjū with ḍamma for agreement with plural wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب أن اقتلوا بكسر النون على أصل التحريك، أو اخرجوا

rows.speaker: حمزة وعاصم
rows.claim: Hamza and Asim read both vowels with kasra, following their original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وعاصم بكسرهما على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use ḍamma, treating the vowels like a hamza joined to the verb.
rows.anchor: والباقون بضمهما إجراء لهما مجرى الهمزة المتصلة بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The few who obeyed were sincere people; the pronoun points to what was prescribed, inferred from the wording, or to one of the two verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: إلا أناس قليل وهم المخلصون. لما بين

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads qalīl as accusative, either as an exception or as an exception meaning only a little action was done.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بالنصب على الاستثناء أو على إلا فعلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing what they are admonished means following and obeying the Messenger willingly and eagerly.
rows.anchor: من متابعة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم مطاوعته طوعا ورغبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such obedience would benefit them in both their immediate and later lives.
rows.anchor: لكان خيرا لهم } في عاجلهم وآجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It would strengthen their religion by producing knowledge and removing doubt.
rows.anchor: في دينهم لأنه أشد لتحصيل العلم ونفي الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the strengthening refers to the reward for their works; the phrase is accusative as a specification.
rows.anchor: أو تثبيتا لثواب أعمالهم ونصبه على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse was also revealed about a hypocritical Jew.
rows.anchor: والآيه أيضا مما نزلت في شأن المنافق اليهودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says this verse and the preceding one concerned Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a's water dispute with al-Zubayr; the Prophet ordered staged irrigation and then told Hatib to let the water flow after al-Zubayr had taken his full right.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها والتي قبلها نزلتا في حاطب بن أبي بلتعة خاصم زبيرا

rows.speaker: حاطب
rows.claim: In the reported dispute, Hatib objected that al-Zubayr was the Prophet's cousin.
rows.anchor: فقال حاطب: لأن كان ابن عمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised immense reward answers an implied question about what follows steadfastness: if they remained steadfast, God would grant it; idha marks result and condition.
rows.anchor: جواب لسؤال مقدر كأنه قيل؛ وما يكون لهم بعد التثبيت فقال وإذا لو تثبتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following a straight path brings them to the divine presence and opens the doors of the unseen.
rows.anchor: يصلون بسلوكه جناب القدس ويفتح عليهم أبواب الغيب

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever acts on what he knows will inherit knowledge of what he did not know.
rows.anchor:
قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من عمل بما علم ورثه الله علم ما لم يعلم "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of joining those God favored encourages obedience by offering companionship with the noblest and most honored people.
rows.anchor: مزيد ترغيب في الطاعة بالوعد عليها مرافقة أكرم الخلائق وأعظمهم قدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four named groups represent ranks in knowledge and action, and the verse urges everyone not to lag behind them.
rows.anchor: قسمهم أربعة أقسام بحسب منازلهم في العلم والعمل، وحث كافة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets complete knowledge and action and go beyond personal perfection to perfecting others.
rows.anchor: الأنبياء الفائزون بكمال العلم والعمل المتجاوزون حد الكمال إلى درجة التكميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truthful ascend through reasoning from proofs and through spiritual purification and discipline to the summit of gnosis, knowing things as they are.
rows.anchor: الصديقون الذين صعدت نفوسهم تارة بمراقي النظر في الحجج والآيات وأخرى بمعارج التصفية والرياضات إلى أوج العرفان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Martyrs' zeal for obedience and publicizing truth led them to give their lives to raise God's word.
rows.anchor: الشهداء الذين أدى بهم الحرص على الطاعة والجد في إظهار الحق حتى بذلوا مهجهم في إعلاء كلمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous devote their lives to obedience and their wealth to what pleases God.
rows.anchor: الصالحون الذين صرفوا أعمارهم في طاعته وأموالهم في مرضاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the favored are knowers of God: prophets attain close vision, while the truthful attain vision from farther away.
rows.anchor: ولك أن تقول المنعم عليهم هم العارفون بالله وهؤلاء إما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the alternative scheme, firmly grounded scholars know through decisive proofs and are God's witnesses on earth, while the righteous rely on indications and persuasions that reassure them.
rows.anchor: والآخرون إما أن يكون عرفانهم بالبراهين القاطعة وهم العلماء الراسخون في العلم الذين هم شهداء الله في أرضه، وإما أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase wa-ḥasuna ulāʾika rafīqan conveys admiration or wonder.
rows.anchor: { وحسن أولئك رفيقا } في معنى التعجب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafīqan is either a specification or circumstantial qualifier; it stays singular because rafīq can describe one or many, or because each person is individually meant.
rows.anchor: نصب على التمييز أو الحال ولم يجمع لأنه يقال للواحد والجمع

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: Thawban, the Prophet's freedman, appeared emaciated and said he was well but missed the Prophet intensely and feared separation in the afterlife because the Prophet would be with the prophets while he might be lower or excluded from Paradise; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاه يوما وقد تغير وجهه ونحل جسمه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika may point to obedient people's reward, extra guidance, and companionship with the favored.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما للمطيعين من الأجر ومزيد الهداية ومرافقة المنعم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dhālika points to the merit and distinction of those whom God favored.
rows.anchor: أو إلى فضل هؤلاء المنعم عليهم ومزيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax may make al-faḍl an adjective of dhālika and min Allāh its predicate, or make al-faḍl the predicate and min Allāh a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: الفضل } صفته. { من الله } خبره أو الفضل خبره ومن الله حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's sufficiency in knowledge refers either to the recompense of those who obey Him or to the measure of grace and who deserves it.
rows.anchor: بجزاء من أطاعه، أو بمقادير الفضل واستحقاق أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage details the general recompense implied by the preceding context: God gathers everyone for judgment, rewarding believers and punishing unbelievers, whose grief is itself torment.
rows.anchor: تفصيل للمجازاة العامة المدلول عليها من فحوى الكلام، وكأنه قال فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا يوم يحشر العباد للمجازاة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof means the miracles and the clear light means the Qur'an; together they are rational signs and transmitted evidence, leaving no excuse.
rows.anchor: عنى بالبرهان المعجزات وبالنور القرآن، أي قد جاءكم دلائل العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported interpretations identify the proof as religion, the Messenger, or the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقيل: البرهان الدين أو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God admits believers who hold fast to Him into a reward corresponding to their faith and deeds, as gracious mercy rather than payment of an obligation.
rows.anchor: في ثواب قدره بإزاء إيمانه وعمله رحمة منه لا قضاء لحق واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised faḍl is an added act of generosity beyond that reward.
rows.anchor: وفضل } إحسان زائد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guiding them to Him means guiding them to God.
rows.anchor: ويهديهم إليه } إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى. وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the destination is the promised reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل إلى الموعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path means Islam and obedience in this world and the road to Paradise in the next.
rows.anchor: صرطا مستقيما } هو الإسلام والطاعة في الدنيا، وطريق الجنة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the question about legal guidance, the phrase about inheritance is omitted because the answer makes it clear that the question concerns kalāla.
rows.anchor: يستفتونك } أي في الكلالة حذفت لدلالة الجواب عليه

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that while he was ill the Prophet visited, and he asked how to dispose of his property as a kalāla; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن جابر بن عبد الله كان مريضا فعاده رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was the last verse revealed among the rulings.
rows.anchor: وهي آخر ما نزل من الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafāʾ and īfāʾ mean fulfilling what a covenant requires; ʿaqd is a firmly bound covenant.
rows.anchor: الوفاء هو القيام بمقتضى العهد وكذلك الإيفاء والعقد العهد الموثق

rows.speaker: الحطيئة
rows.claim: Al-Hutay'a's line about people securing a neighbor's contract illustrates the word ʿaqd.
rows.anchor:
قال الحطيئة:
قوم إذا عقدوا عقدا لجارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root image of a contract is joining two things so firmly that they are difficult to separate.
rows.anchor: وأصله الجمع بين الشيئين بحيث يعسر الانفصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenants include God's obligations to His servants and agreements between people, such as trusts and transactions.
rows.anchor: ما يعم العقود التي عقدها الله سبحانه وتعالى على عباده وألزمها إياهم من التكاليف، وما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duties are obligatory, or include recommended agreements if the command is understood to cover both obligation and recommendation.
rows.anchor: مما يجب الوفاء به، أو يحسن إن حملنا الأمر على المشترك بين الوجوب والندب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bahīma can mean any living creature unable to distinguish, or, according to another definition, any four-footed animal.
rows.anchor: والبهيمة كل حي لا يميز. وقيل كل ذات أربع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive means animals belonging to livestock, like saying a garment of silk; it includes the eight livestock pairs, with gazelles and wild cattle appended.
rows.anchor: ومعناه البهيمة من الأنعام. وهي الأزواج الثمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, bahīma refers to gazelles, wild cattle, and similar animals, attached to livestock by resemblance in cud-chewing and lack of canines.
rows.anchor: في الاجترار وعدم الأنياب، وإضافتها إلى الأنعام لملابسة الشبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means the forbidden matters recited to you, such as carrion, or things whose prohibition is recited.
rows.anchor: إلا محرم ما يتلى عليكم كقوله تعالى: { حرمت عليكم الميتة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not making game lawful can describe the state of the pronoun in lakum or the subject of awfū; treating it as an exception is strained.
rows.anchor: حال من الضمير في { لكم } وقيل من واو { أوفوا } وقيل استثناء وفيه تعسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣayd may mean the act of hunting or the hunted animal.
rows.anchor: الصيد } يحتمل المصدر والمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase while you are consecrated is circumstantial, and ḥurum is the plural of ḥarām, an uncompleted pilgrim.
rows.anchor: أنتم حرم } حال مما استكن في { محلي } ، وال { حرم } جمع حرام وهو المحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God decides whatever He wills to permit or prohibit.
rows.anchor: إن الله يحكم ما يريد } من تحليل أو تحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The symbols of God mean the pilgrimage rites: the word denotes something made a marker, and these rites mark the pilgrimage and its stations.
rows.anchor: يعني مناسك الحج، جمع شعيرة وهي اسم ما أشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is God's religion, as in 22:32, where honoring God's symbols means honoring His religion.
rows.anchor:
ومن يعظم شعئر الله
[الحج: 32] أي دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is the obligations God prescribed for His servants.
rows.anchor: وقيل فرائضه التي حدها لعباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not violating the sacred month means not fighting in it or manipulating it through intercalation.
rows.anchor: الشهر الحرام } بالقتال فيه أو بالنسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hady refers to what is offered to the Kaaba; the plural hady is formed like jadī from jadiyya.
rows.anchor: ولا الهدي } ما أهدي إلى الكعبة، جمع هدية كجدي في جميع جدية السرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qalāʾid may mean the garlanded sacrificial animals, singled out as the noblest offerings, or the garlands themselves as an emphatic prohibition.
rows.anchor: أي ذوات القلائد من الهدي، وعطفها على الهدي للاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with 24:31 supports mentioning the garlands themselves; sandals, bark, and other garlands marked offerings so people would not molest them.
rows.anchor: والقلائد جمع قلادة وهي ما قلد به الهدي من نعل أو لحاء شجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those heading to the Sacred House are people intending to visit it.
rows.anchor: ولا آمين البيت الحرام } قاصدين لزيارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking favor means seeking God's reward and approval; the clause is circumstantial, not adjectival, because an adjectival participle does not govern, and it warns against attacking them and signals a reason to refrain.
rows.anchor: أن يثيبهم ويرضى عنهم، والجملة في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says they sought trade income and only claimed to seek God's approval; the verse descended during the Hudaybiya pilgrimage year when Muslims considered attacking them because al-Hutaym had raided Medina's herds, so the verse was abrogated.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه يبتغون من الله رزقا بالتجارة ورضوانا بزعمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has tabtaghūn, addressing the believers directly.
rows.anchor: وقرىء تبتغون على خطاب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After leaving ihram, hunting is permitted; the command after a prohibition here does not establish that every later command after prohibition means permission.
rows.anchor: وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا } إذن في الاصطياد بعد زوال الإحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading places kasra on the fā of faṣṭādū by transferring the connecting vowel, a very weak reading.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بكسر الفاء على إلقاء حركة الوصل عليها وهو ضعيف جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading aḥlaltum is also given; both ḥalla and aḥalla are used for a pilgrim leaving consecration.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «أحللتم» يقال حل المحرم وأحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yajrimanakum means either do not let it drive you or do not let it cause you to incur something.
rows.anchor: ولا يجرمنكم } لا يحملنكم أو لا يكسبنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shanaʾān means the intensity of hatred and hostility; it is a verbal noun annexed to its object or subject.
rows.anchor: شدة بغضهم وعداوتهم وهو مصدر أضيف إلى المفعول أو الفاعل

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وإسماعيل عن نافع وابن عياش عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Isma'il from Nafi, and Ibn Ayyash from Asim read shanaʾān with a still nūn; it can be a verbal noun or an adjective meaning hateful.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وإسماعيل عن نافع وابن عياش عن عاصم بسكون النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fَعلان form is more frequent as an adjective, as in ʿaṭshān and sakrān.
rows.anchor: وفعلان في النعت أكثر كعطشان وسكران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reason is that they barred the believers from the Sacred Mosque in the year of Hudaybiya.
rows.anchor: أن صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام } لأن صدوكم عنه عام الحديبية

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the hamza of an with kasra, making it an interrupting conditional whose response is supplied by lā yajrimanakum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بكسر الهمزة على أنه شرط معترض أغنى عن جوابه لا يجرمنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An taʿtadū means retaliating and is the second object of yajrimanakum, which can take one or two objects like kasaba.
rows.anchor: أن تعتدوا } بالانتقام، وهو ثاني مفعولي يجرمنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the reading yujrimannakum, the verb is causative, shifted from one object to two by the hamza.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ { يجرمنكم } بضم الياء جعله منقولا من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cooperation in righteousness and piety means pardoning, overlooking, following the command, and resisting one's desires.
rows.anchor: على العفو والإغضاء ومتابعة الأمر ومجانبة الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cooperation in sin and aggression means joining in gratification and revenge.
rows.anchor: للتشفي والانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should fear God because His retaliation is more severe.
rows.anchor: واتقوا الله إن الله شديد آلعقاب } فانتقامه أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The necessity exception in 2:173 means God does not hold a person accountable for eating forbidden food under that exception.
rows.anchor: غير باغ ولا عاد [البقرة: 173] { فإن الله غفور رحيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the question contains the sense of saying, mādhā takes a full clause as its complement; the word mādhā has been discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: لما تضمن السؤال معنى القول أوقع على الجملة، وقد سبق الكلام في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says alayhim rather than ʿalaynā to preserve the indirect third-person form of yasʾalūnaka, though either wording is idiomatic.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال لهم ولم يقل لنا على الحكاية، لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask about permitted foods because, after hearing what was forbidden, they wanted to know what was allowed.
rows.anchor: والمسؤول ما أحل لهم من المطاعم كأنهم لما تلي عليهم ما حرم عليهم سألوا عما أحل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wholesome are things that sound natures do not find repugnant.
rows.anchor: ما لم تستخبثه الطباع السليمة ولم تنفر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One implication is that whatever Arabs consider repulsive is prohibited.
rows.anchor: ومن مفهومه حرم مستخبثات العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, wholesome means foods for which neither a text nor an analogy establishes prohibition.
rows.anchor: أو ما لم يدل نص ولا قياس على حرمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about what you have trained can be a relative clause coordinated with wholesome foods, implying game caught by what you trained, or a conditional clause whose answer is eat.
rows.anchor: عطف على { الطيبات } إن جعلت { ما } موصولة على تقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawāriḥ are animals that catch prey for their owners, including predatory quadrupeds and birds.
rows.anchor: كواسب الصيد على أهلها من سباع ذوات الأربع والطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukallibīn means trainers who discipline hunting animals; the term derives from dogs because they are commonly trained this way or because every predator is called a dog, and it is circumstantial to stress training.
rows.anchor: مكلبين } معلمين إياه الصيد، والمكلب مؤدب الجوارح

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet's supplication that God set one of His dogs on a man supports calling every predator a dog.
rows.anchor: " اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God taught includes hunting tricks and training methods, whether inspired by God, acquired through God-given reason, or taught as God's rules for how the animal follows, responds, returns, and holds prey for its owner.
rows.anchor: من الحيل وطرق التأديب، فإن العلم بها إلهام من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim not to eat prey if the hunting animal ate from it, because it caught that prey for itself.
rows.anchor:
لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لعدي بن حاتم
" وإن أكل منه فلا تأكل

rows.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
rows.claim: Most jurists hold that one may eat only what the trained animal did not eat.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب أكثر الفقهاء

rows.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
rows.claim: Some jurists do not require this condition for predatory birds because they cannot realistically be trained to that degree.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: لا يشترط ذلك في سباع الطير لأن

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other jurists do not require the condition at all.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون لا يشترط مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in remembering God's name may refer to the trained animal, with invocation at release, or to the prey, with invocation when slaughtering it after capture.
rows.anchor: الضمير لما علمتم والمعنى: سموا عليه عند إرساله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-consciousness here means observing God's prohibitions; He quickly reckons and holds people to account for both major and minor matters.
rows.anchor: واتقوا الله } في محرماته. { إن الله سريع الحساب } فيؤاخذكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worse than that means worse than the thing being condemned in the preceding context.
rows.anchor: قل هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلك } أي من ذلك المنقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathūbah normally means a reward, unlike punishment, but here it stands ironically for punishment as in the cited saying; it is accusative as a specification of worse.
rows.anchor: والمثوبة مختصة بالخير كالعقوبة بالشر فوضعت ها هنا موضعها على طريقة قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about those whom God cursed may be an apposition to worse, with an omitted annex, or mean that their religion is worse, or be the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: بدل من بشر على حذف مضاف أي بشر من أهل ذلك من لعنه الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people meant are Jews, distanced from God's mercy and angered for disbelief and persistent sin after clear signs.
rows.anchor: وهم اليهود أبعدهم الله من رحمته وسخط عليهم بكفرهم وانهماكهم في المعاصي بعد وضوح الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some were transformed into apes, namely the Sabbath people, and some into pigs, the unbelievers among Jesus's table community.
rows.anchor: ومسخ بعضهم قردة وهم أصحاب السبت، وبعضهم خنازير وهم كفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places both transformations among the Sabbath people, with young people changed into apes and elders into pigs.
rows.anchor: وقيل كلا المسخين في أصحاب السبت مسخت شبانهم قردة ومشايخهم خنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one reading, ʿabada al-ṭāghūt coordinates with the relative clause and is passive; the raised ṭāghūt means it became worshipped, with an omitted reference to among them.
rows.anchor: وعبد الطغوت } عطف على صلة من وكذا { عبد الطغوت } على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings are ʿābidi al-ṭāghūt, an adjective, or ʿabada as a plural; one reading is genitive and attaches to man.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ «وعابد الطاغوت» أو { عبد } على أنه نعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭāghūt may refer to the calf, soothsayers, or anyone they obey in disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: والمراد { من } الطاغوت العجل وقيل الكهنة وكل من أطاعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those people are the ones cursed by God.
rows.anchor: أولئك } أي الملعونون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their place is called worse to intensify the indication of their wickedness.
rows.anchor: شر مكانا } جعل مكانهم شرا ليكون أبلغ في الدلالة على شرارتهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, makānan means the place to which they turn or return.
rows.anchor: وقيل { مكانا } منصرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the balanced way between Christian excess and Jewish disparagement; the comparative forms mean increased wickedness and error absolutely, not relative to believers.
rows.anchor: قصد الطريق المتوسط بين غلو النصارى وقدح اليهود، والمراد من صيغتي التفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that they come saying they believe was revealed about hypocritical Jews, or according to another view about hypocrites generally.
rows.anchor: نزلت في يهود نافقوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو في عامة المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering and leaving in disbelief means they leave the Prophet unchanged by what they heard.
rows.anchor: أي يخرجون من عندك كما دخلوا لم يؤثر فيهم ما سمعوا منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses are circumstantial descriptions of those speaking; bi-l-kufri and bihi are states tied to their entry and exit.
rows.anchor: والجملتان حالان من فاعل قالوا وبالكفر وبه حالان من فاعلي دخلوا وخرجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qad makes the past approach the present and signals expectation, suggesting the signs of hypocrisy were visible and the Prophet suspected them.
rows.anchor: وقد وإن دخلت لتقريب الماضي من الحال ليصح أن يقع حالا أفادت أيضا لما فيها من التوقع أن أمارة النفاق كانت لائحة عليهم، وكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the disbelief they conceal, a threat against them.
rows.anchor: والله أعلم بما كانوا يكتمون } أي من الكفر، وفيه وعيد لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥurum means people in consecration; ḥarām has plural ḥurum like ridāḥ has plural ridaḥ.
rows.anchor: وأنتم حرم } أي محرمون جمع حرام كرداح وردح،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names killing rather than ritual slaughter to make the prohibition comprehensive.
rows.anchor: ولعله ذكر القتل دون الذبح والذكاة للتعميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Game here likely means edible prey, as that is the customary sense.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالصيد ما يؤكل لحمه لأنه الغالب فيه عرفا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet exempted five harmful animals from the rule, naming the kite, crow, scorpion, mouse, and vicious dog.
rows.anchor: خمس يقتلن في الحل والحرم، الحدأة والغراب والعقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another narration substitutes the snake for the scorpion; the report also indicates that every harmful animal may be killed.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى «الحية» بدل «العقرب»، مع ما فيه من التنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists disagree whether the prohibition invalidates ritual slaughter, making the pilgrim's slaughter like carrion or an idolater's slaughter, or whether it remains valid like a usurper slaughtering a stolen sheep.
rows.anchor: واختلف في أن هذا النهي هل يلغي حكم الذبح فيلحق مذبوح المحرم بالميتة ومذبوح الوثني أو لا فيكون كالشاة المغصوبة إذا ذبحها الغاصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intentional means remembering one's consecration and knowing the prohibition before killing.
rows.anchor: ذاكرا لإحرامه عالما بأنه حرام عليه قبل ما يقتله

rows.speaker: أكثر
rows.claim: Most jurists say intention does not limit compensation, since intentional and mistaken destruction alike entail liability; intention instead supports the threat for repeat offenses and fits the occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: واحد في إيجاب الضمان، بل لقوله: { ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion was a wild donkey that appeared during the Hudaybiya lesser pilgrimage; Abu al-Yusr killed it with his spear, and the verse came down.
rows.anchor: إذ روي: أنه عن لهم في عمرة الحديبية حمار وحش فطعنه أبو اليسر

rows.speaker: الكوفيون ويعقوب
rows.claim: The Kufans and Yaqub read the nominative jazāʾ with accusative mithl, meaning a compensation equivalent to the prey from livestock is due.
rows.anchor: برفع الجزاء، والمثل قراءة الكوفيين ويعقوب بمعنى فعليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this reading the prepositional phrase does not attach directly to jazāʾ because an intervening adjective separates the verbal noun from its complement.
rows.anchor: وعليه لا يتعلق الجار بجزاء للفصل بينهما بالصفة فإن متعلق المصدر كالصلة له فلا يوصف ما لم يتم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers construe the verbal noun with its object and insert mithl, meaning the offender must compensate an equivalent of what was killed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون على إضافة المصدر إلى المفعول وإقحام مثلي كما في قولهم مثلي لا يقول كذا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading puts both jazāʾ and mithl in the accusative, meaning let him pay an equivalent compensation or that his compensation is the equivalent.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فجزاء مثلي ما قتل بنصبهما على فليجز جزاء، أو فعليه أن يجزي جزاء

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafi'i measure equivalence by the animal's physical form and shape.
rows.anchor: وهذه المماثلة باعتبار الخلقة والهيئة عند مالك والشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa measures equivalence by value and values the prey where it was killed.
rows.anchor: والقيمة عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى وقال: يقوم الصيد حيث صيد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: If the value reaches the price of a sacrificial animal, he may offer livestock, buy food and distribute the specified shares, or fast a day per poor person; if lower, he chooses feeding or fasting. The wording better fits the first view.
rows.anchor: فإن بلغت القيمة ثمن هدى تخير بين أن يهدي ما قيمته قيمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two just arbiters qualify the compensation or describe its state; evaluation and physical matching both require judgment and effort.
rows.anchor: يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم } صفة جزاء ويحتمل أن يكون حالا من ضميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading uses singular dhū ʿadl, understood generically or as the ruler.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ذو عدل» على إرادة الجنس أو الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadʾyan may be circumstantial with respect to the pronoun in bihi or jazāʾ, or an apposition to mithl in its syntactic case or wording.
rows.anchor: هديا } حال من الهاء في به أو من جزاء وإن نون لتخصصه بالصفة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacrificial offering reaching the Kaaba means slaughtering it in the sanctuary and distributing it to the poor there.
rows.anchor: بلغ الكعبة } وصف به هديا لأن إضافته لفظية ومعنى بلوغه الكعبة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires slaughter in the sanctuary but allows distribution wherever desired.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة يذبح بالحرم ويتصدق به حيث شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aw kaffārah coordinates with jazāʾ when jazāʾ is nominative; if accusative, an omitted predicate is understood.
rows.anchor: أو كفارة } عطف على جزاء إن رفعته وإن نصبته فخبر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿāmu miskīn may clarify or replace kaffārah, or be the predicate of an omitted clause.
rows.anchor: طعام مسكين } عطف بيان أو بدل منه، أو خبر محذوف أي هي طعام

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read kaffāratu ṭaʿāmi in genitive construction to specify the expiation, like a ring of silver.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر كفارة { طعام } بالإضافة للتبيين كقولك: خاتم فضة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: According to al-Shafi'i, expiation feeds poor people staple food worth the sacrificial animal, giving each a mudd.
rows.anchor: والمعنى عند الشافعي أو أن يكفر بإطعام مساكين ما يساوي قيمة الهدي من غالب قوت البلد فيعطي كل مسكين مدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting equal to the food means one day of fasting for each poor person; ʿadl is a verbal noun used for its object.
rows.anchor: أو ما ساواه من الصوم فيصوم عن طعام كل مسكين يوما، وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kasra reading of ʿadl means an equivalent in measure, like an equivalent load; dhālika refers to the food and ṣiyāman specifies the equivalence.
rows.anchor: بكسر العين وهو ما عدل بالشيء في المقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause means the offender must pay compensation, feed, or fast so that he tastes the burden and bad outcome of violating the sacred state.
rows.anchor: وبال أمره } متعلق بمحذوف أي فعليه الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wabal originally means weight, hence the phrase also means a severe burden for violating God's command.
rows.anchor: أو الثقل الشديد على مخالفة أمر الله تعالى وأصل الوبل الثقل ومنه الطعام الوبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God pardoned earlier hunting violations committed before the prohibition, before it took effect, or on this first occasion.
rows.anchor: عفا الله عما سلف } من قتل الصيد محرما في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning means repeating the offense; God's threat does not bar expiation for repeat offenders, despite what is attributed to Ibn Abbas and Shurayh.
rows.anchor: ومن عاد } إلى مثل هذا. { فينتقم الله منه } فهو ينتقم الله منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وشريح
rows.claim: A view attributed to Ibn Abbas and Shurayh denies expiation for a repeat offender.
rows.anchor: كما حكي عن ابن عباس وشريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty and takes vengeance on those who persist in disobedience.
rows.anchor: والله عزيز ذو انتقام } مما أصر على عصيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking whose everything in the heavens and earth is means who created and owns it; the question rebukes its hearers.
rows.anchor: قل لمن ما في السموات والأرض } خلقا وملكا، وهو سؤال تبكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their answer that it belongs to God confirms the point and shows that only He can be named in response.
rows.anchor: قل لله } تقريرا لهم وتنبيها على أنه المتعين للجواب بالإنفاق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God graciously undertook mercy for Himself; it includes both worlds and guidance to know Him, recognize His oneness through proofs, receive scripture, and be given respite despite disbelief.
rows.anchor: كتب على نفسه الرحمة } التزمها تفضلا وإحسانا والمراد بالرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about gathering is a resumed oath and threat against shirk and failure to reflect; it can mean resurrection from graves until the Day, or gathering on that day with ilā meaning fī.
rows.anchor: ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيمة } استئناف وقسم للوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, gathering is a partial apposition to mercy, since resurrecting people is itself one of God's mercies to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل بدل من الرحمة بدل البعض فإنه من رحمته بعثه إياكم وإنعامه عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase no doubt refers either to the Day or to the gathering.
rows.anchor: لا ريب فيه } في اليوم أو الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who lost themselves squandered their original nature and sound reason, their capital.
rows.anchor: الذين خسروا أنفسهم } بتضييع رأس مالهم. وهو الفطرة الأصلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax of alladhīna may be accusative as a phrase of censure, nominative as predicate, or a topic whose predicate is they do not believe.
rows.anchor: وموضع الذين نصب على الذم أو رفع على الخبر أي: وأنتم الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in they do not believe shows causation: following senses and illusion, blind imitation, and neglecting reflection ruined their reason, leading to persistent rejection of faith.
rows.anchor: والفاء للدلالة على أن عدم إيمانهم مسبب عن خسرانهم، فإن إبطال العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase wa-lahu is coordinated with lillāh.
rows.anchor: وله } عطف على لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakana may mean dwelled, so the phrase covers all that night and day contain, as in 14:45.
rows.anchor: ما سكن فى اليل والنهار } من السكنى وتعديته بفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, sakana derives from stillness and names both what rests and what moves, one of two opposites standing for the other.
rows.anchor: أو من السكون أي ما سكن فيهما وتحرك فاكتفى بأحد الضدين عن الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears everything audible and knows everything known; the wording may warn the polytheists about their speech and acts.
rows.anchor: وهو السميع } لكل مسموع. { العليم } بكل معلوم فلا يخفى عليه شيء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase from before you, min is extra, so the meaning is simply before you.
rows.anchor: إلى أمم من قبلك } أي قبلك، ومن زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being seized means God seized them after they disbelieved and denied the messengers.
rows.anchor: فكفروا وكذبوا المرسلين فأخذناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-baʾsāʾ means hardship and poverty.
rows.anchor: بالبأساء } بالشدة والفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍarrāʾ means harm and afflictions; both are feminine forms with no corresponding masculine form.
rows.anchor: والضراء } والضر والآفات وهما صيغتا تأنيث لا مذكر لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose was that they humble themselves before God and repent from their sins.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يتضرعون } يتذللون لنا ويتوبون عن ذنوبهم
